children: Microsoft, the cloud and software giant

, unveiled a push to run AI directly on PCs, with shares up approximately 1.4% to $529.97 at around 10:25 a.m. ET Friday. The package combines local AI models, tighter controls on desktop agents and a premium Surface laptop. The pitch is simple: put more computing power on the desk while keeping the cloud in the loop.

According to Reuters, Microsoft Execution Containers limit what desktop agents can access, while Copilot splits tasks between the device and the cloud. The Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599 and tops out at $5,899. Anthropic, OpenAI and Nvidia
plan to use the security technology. Those controls matter: an agent that can act on a computer needs clear boundaries around files, applications and sensitive information.

The valuation graphic puts Microsoft 10.38% below its $591.37 GF Value estimate, suggesting upside without guaranteeing it. The business trade-off is sharper. Local AI can deliver faster responses and keep sensitive data on the device, but it can also reduce demand for some Azure inference workloads. Microsoft needs stronger Windows adoption, premium-device sales and continued cloud usage to make that shift pay.

title: Microsoft Stocks Rise 1.4% as Local AI Shifts Compute Off Azure
